entries.notes: Plain alternative: tetsudau (tetsudatte = help me).

entries.use: Parents, teachers and dog owners say it daily, usually without o: zenzen iu koto kikanai (won't listen at all). Also for a body or machine that won't cooperate (karada ga iu koto kikanai). It's obeying, not just hearing someone out (hanashi o kiku).

example.romaji: uchi no ko, zenzen iu koto kikanai no.
example.ja: うちの子、全然言うこと聞かないの。
example.english: My kid won't listen to a word I say.

examplePolite.romaji: uchi no ko, zenzen iu koto o kikanai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: うちの子、全然言うことを聞かないんです。
examplePolite.english: My kid won't listen to a word I say.

entries.notes: Parents' command: iu koto kikinasai.

entries.english: hit, lay a finger on; get into (drugs, stocks); make a move on (someone)
entries.use: Mostly heard as a warning or in a fight: te o dasu na (hands off), saki ni te o dashita (threw the first punch). It also means getting into something new (kabu ni te o dasu) or making a move on someone. Literally it's also 'hold out your hand' (te o dashite). Don't mix it up with kuchi o dasu (butt in) or kao o dasu (show up).

example.romaji: saki ni te dashita no wa mukou da yo.
example.ja: 先に手出したのは向こうだよ。
example.english: They're the ones who threw the first punch.

examplePolite.romaji: saki ni te o dashita no wa mukou desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 先に手を出したのは向こうですよ。
examplePolite.english: They're the ones who threw the first punch.

entries.notes: Noun: tedashi (tedashi suru na = keep out of it).

entries.use: Said when someone has done you a favour you haven't repaid: ano hito ni wa kari ga aru. kari ga dekita (now I owe you) and kari o kaesu (pay it back) go with it; it's mostly favours, since a money debt is usually shakkin ga aru.

example.romaji: ano hito ni wa kari ga aru kara, kotowarenai.
example.ja: あの人には借りがあるから、断れない。
example.english: I owe him one, so I can't say no.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito ni wa kari ga aru node, kotowarenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの人には借りがあるので、断れないんです。
examplePolite.english: I owe him one, so I can't say no.

entries.notes: Flip side: kashi ga aru / kore de kashi hitotsu ne (now you owe me one). Even again: kore de kashikari nashi.

entries.use: The go-to offer of support when someone is struggling, mostly in the potential: chikara ni nareru koto attara itte, or chikara ni narenakute gomen. It covers any help at all; te o kasu is a quick hand and chikara o kasu is backing something big.

example.romaji: nanka chikara ni nareru koto attara itte ne.
example.ja: なんか力になれることあったら言ってね。
example.english: If there's anything I can do, just say.

examplePolite.romaji: nanika chikara ni nareru koto ga attara, itte kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 何か力になれることがあったら、言ってくださいね。
examplePolite.english: If there's anything I can do, just say.

entries.english: deal with, take on (an opponent); (negative) ignore, not bother with
entries.use: Two everyday uses. In the negative it means ignoring someone: aite ni shinakute ii (just ignore him), daremo aite ni shite kurenai (nobody pays me any attention), aite ni sarenai (get brushed off). In the positive it means dealing with or taking someone on: kodomo o aite ni suru shigoto (a job dealing with kids), dare o aite ni shiteru to omotteru no? (who do you think you're dealing with?). Don't confuse it with ate ni suru (count on).

example.romaji: anna yatsu, aite ni shinakute ii yo.
example.ja: あんなやつ、相手にしなくていいよ。
example.english: Just ignore a guy like that.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito no koto wa, aite ni shinakute ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの人のことは、相手にしなくていいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Just ignore him.

entries.notes: aite o suru (with o) = keep someone company, play with (kids).

entries.use: Warm concern for how a person is doing, heard most as thanks: itsumo ki ni kakete kurete arigatou (thanks for always looking out for me). Not ki ni suru (mind, worry about), which is fretting over a thing.

example.romaji: itsumo ki ni kakete kurete, arigatou ne.
example.ja: いつも気にかけてくれて、ありがとうね。
example.english: Thanks for always looking out for me.

examplePolite.romaji: itsumo ki ni kakete itadaite, arigatou gozaimasu.
examplePolite.ja: いつも気にかけていただいて、ありがとうございます。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for always looking out for me.

entries.notes: Also for your own health: kenkou o ki ni kakeru (watch your health).

entries.use: A complaint or warning about interfering in someone's decisions: kuchi dasanaide (stay out of it), oya ga sugu kuchi o dasu. Unlike kuchi o hasamu (cut into a conversation), it's meddling in what isn't yours to decide.

example.romaji: kore wa watashi no mondai da kara, kuchi dasanaide.
example.ja: これは私の問題だから、口出さないで。
example.english: This is my problem, so stay out of it.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa watashi no mondai desu kara, kuchi o dasanaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: これは私の問題ですから、口を出さないでください。
examplePolite.english: This is my problem, so please stay out of it.

entries.notes: Noun: kuchidashi (kuchidashi shinaide).

entries.english: speak to someone, be on speaking terms
entries.use: Mostly negative, after a fight: mou kuchi kikanai (I'm not speaking to you), kuchi kiite kurenai (she won't talk to me); also namaiki na kuchi o kiku na (don't talk back). The kiku is 利く (work), so it isn't iu koto o kiku (obey).

example.romaji: kenka shite kara, kanojo ga kuchi kiite kurenai.
example.ja: 喧嘩してから、彼女が口きいてくれない。
example.english: Since our fight, she won't speak to me.

examplePolite.romaji: kenka shite kara, kanojo ga kuchi o kiite kurenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 喧嘩してから、彼女が口をきいてくれないんです。
examplePolite.english: Since our fight, she won't speak to me.

entries.notes: Also kuchi o kiite morau = get someone to put in a good word.

entries.use: Mostly in warnings and complaints: anmari ate ni shinaide (don't count on me too much), ano hito wa ate ni naranai (he's unreliable). Also for forecasts and promises; not aite ni suru (bother with someone).

example.romaji: anmari ate ni shinaide ne.
example.ja: あんまり当てにしないでね。
example.english: Don't count on me too much, OK?

examplePolite.romaji: amari ate ni shinaide kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: あまり当てにしないでくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please don't count on me too much.

entries.notes: ate ni naranai = unreliable; plain alternative: tayoru.

entries.use: The snappy comeback to advice nobody asked for, usually yokei na osewa da (yo). Said to friends, family or rivals, never to someone above you; osewa here is sarcastic, unlike thankful osewa ni naru.

example.romaji: yokei na osewa da yo. hottoite.
example.ja: 余計なお世話だよ。ほっといて。
example.english: None of your business. Leave me alone.

entries.notes: Variant: ookina osewa (da).

entries.use: Popping into a party, club, office or someone's home, often briefly: chotto kao dasu ne. Not te o dasu or kuchi o dasu, which are about interfering.

example.romaji: nomikai, chotto dake kao dasu yo.
example.ja: 飲み会、ちょっとだけ顔出すよ。
example.english: I'll show my face at the drinks for a bit.

examplePolite.romaji: nomikai ni wa, chotto dake kao o dashimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 飲み会には、ちょっとだけ顔を出します。
examplePolite.english: I'll show my face at the drinks for a bit.

entries.notes: Also kao o miseru, the usual one for visiting: tama ni wa kao misete ne (come and see us sometimes).

entries.english: we all need help sometimes; you'd do the same for me
entries.use: The reflex reply when a neighbour, colleague or friend thanks you or apologises for needing help: iie, otagaisama desu yo. It says the help runs both ways, so nobody owes anyone; the full line is komatta toki wa otagaisama.

example.romaji: ii tte, otagaisama da yo.
example.ja: いいって、お互い様だよ。
example.english: Don't mention it, you'd do the same for me.

examplePolite.romaji: iie, komatta toki wa otagaisama desu kara.
examplePolite.ja: いいえ、困ったときはお互い様ですから。
examplePolite.english: Not at all, we all need help sometimes.

entries.notes: Close: mochitsu motaretsu (give and take).

entries.use: For friends, colleagues or partners you naturally click with (ki ga au hito), often negative too (joushi to ki ga awanai). The au is 合う (fit), not 会う (meet); don't confuse it with ki ga aru (be into someone).

example.romaji: kanojo to wa nanka ki ga au n da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼女とはなんか気が合うんだよね。
example.english: I just click with her somehow.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo to wa nanka ki ga au n desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女とはなんか気が合うんですよね。
examplePolite.english: I just click with her somehow.

entries.notes: Negative ki ga awanai = just don't get on. Near-twin: uma ga au.

entries.english: poke your nose in, get mixed up in
entries.use: A warning or complaint about getting involved in what isn't yours: yokei na koto ni kubi tsukkomu na. Unlike kuchi o dasu (butting in with advice), you actually wade in.

example.romaji: yokei na koto ni kubi tsukkomanai hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: 余計なことに首突っ込まないほうがいいよ。
example.english: Better not stick your nose in other people's business.

examplePolite.romaji: yokei na koto ni wa kubi o tsukkomanai hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 余計なことには首を突っ込まないほうがいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: It's better not to get mixed up in other people's business.

entries.politeJa: なかったことにします
entries.literal: make it a thing that wasn't
entries.use: After an awkward moment, a confession or a slip: ima no, nakatta koto ni shite (forget I said that); also for burying a mistake or a deal. It erases rather than forgives, unlike mizu ni nagasu.

example.romaji: ima no, nakatta koto ni shite.
example.ja: 今の、なかったことにして。
example.english: Forget I said that.

examplePolite.romaji: ima no wa, nakatta koto ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今のは、なかったことにしてください。
examplePolite.english: Please forget I said that.

entries.english: put yourself in the other person's place
entries.use: Advice from parents, teachers and friends, almost always aite no mi ni natte kangaete (think how they'd feel). Any person can stand in for aite: kodomo no mi ni natte. It's imagining one person's side; kuuki o yomu is sensing the room.

example.romaji: aite no mi ni natte kangaete mina yo.
example.ja: 相手の身になって考えてみなよ。
example.english: Try seeing it from their side.

examplePolite.romaji: aite no mi ni natte kangaete mite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 相手の身になって考えてみてください。
examplePolite.english: Please try to see it from their side.

entries.notes: Also aite no tachiba ni natte (from their position).

entries.english: hold others back, let the team down; (deliberately) drag someone down
entries.use: The team, club and work apology ashi hippatte gomen, and also deliberate sabotage of a rival: hito no ashi bakkari hipparu (always dragging others down). A false friend: English 'pull someone's leg' means tease. ashidematoi ni naru is being a burden just by being there.

example.romaji: minna no ashi hippatte, gomen ne.
example.ja: みんなの足引っ張って、ごめんね。
example.english: Sorry for holding everyone back.

examplePolite.romaji: minasan no ashi o hippatte shimatte, sumimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 皆さんの足を引っ張ってしまって、すみません。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry for holding everyone back.

entries.use: Gossip about who fancies whom, always X ni ki ga aru: ano ko, kimi ni ki ga aru yo. Without ni it means being willing (yaru ki ga aru); don't confuse it with ki ga au (get along).

example.romaji: kare, zettai kimi ni ki ga aru yo.
example.ja: 彼、絶対君に気があるよ。
example.english: He's definitely into you.

examplePolite.romaji: kare, zettai satou-san ni ki ga arimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼、絶対佐藤さんに気がありますよ。
examplePolite.english: He's definitely into you, Ms Sato.

entries.notes: Negative ki ga nai = not interested.

entries.english: be a handful, need constant looking after
entries.use: Fond grumbling about a child, partner, junior or pet who keeps needing help: mattaku, sewa ga yakeru na. There's affection in it; mendokusai is plain annoyance.

example.romaji: mattaku, sewa ga yakeru na.
example.ja: まったく、世話が焼けるな。
example.english: Honestly, you're such a handful.

examplePolite.romaji: uchi no musuko wa, hontou ni sewa ga yakeru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: うちの息子は、本当に世話が焼けるんです。
examplePolite.english: My son is such a handful.

entries.notes: sewa o yaku = fuss over someone; a born fusser is a sewayaki.

entries.english: read the mood, pick up on the vibe
entries.use: Mostly a complaint about someone who doesn't: kuuki yomenai (he can't read the room), kuuki yome yo (read the room!). It's sensing the mood; ki o tsukau is actively being considerate.

example.romaji: ano hito, honto kuuki yomenai yo ne.
example.ja: あの人、ほんと空気読めないよね。
example.english: He really can't read the room, can he?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito, hontou ni kuuki yomenai desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人、本当に空気読めないですよね。
examplePolite.english: He really can't read the room, can he?

entries.english: encourage someone to go for it
entries.use: Thanking or describing someone who gave you the courage to act, usually -te kureta: ano hito ga senaka o oshite kureta. Different from kata o motsu, which is taking someone's side in a dispute.

example.romaji: tomodachi ga senaka oshite kureta n da.
example.ja: 友達が背中押してくれたんだ。
example.english: My friend gave me the push I needed.

examplePolite.romaji: tomodachi ga senaka o oshite kureta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 友達が背中を押してくれたんです。
examplePolite.english: My friend gave me the push I needed.

entries.politeJa: お言葉に甘えさせていただきます
entries.english: I'll gladly take you up on that
entries.englishIdiom: I'll take you up on that
entries.use: The fixed way to accept an offer (a ride, a treat, staying over) after first holding back: jaa, okotoba ni amaete. Said to hosts, seniors and colleagues, and jokingly to friends.

example.romaji: ii no? jaa, okotoba ni amaete!
example.ja: いいの？じゃあ、お言葉に甘えて！
example.english: Really? Well, if you insist!

examplePolite.romaji: ii n desu ka? jaa, okotoba ni amaesasete itadakimasu.
examplePolite.ja: いいんですか？じゃあ、お言葉に甘えさせていただきます。
examplePolite.english: Are you sure? Then I'll gladly take you up on it.

entries.use: Said admiringly about someone with a big network, often when you need a contact: kare, kao ga hiroi kara. Nothing to do with a big face (kao ga ookii).

example.romaji: kare, kao ga hiroi kara kiite miru yo.
example.ja: 彼、顔が広いから聞いてみるよ。
example.english: He knows everyone, I'll ask him.

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa kao ga hiroi node, kiite mimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼は顔が広いので、聞いてみますね。
examplePolite.english: He knows everyone, so I'll ask him.

entries.kana: いっしょうのおねがい
entries.english: please, I'm begging you (just this once)
entries.use: The dramatic plea among friends and siblings, or from kids to parents, often with hands pressed together: isshou no onegai! Everyone uses it again and again despite the name, which is half the joke.

example.romaji: isshou no onegai! kondo dake okane kashite.
example.ja: 一生のお願い！今度だけお金貸して。
example.english: I'm begging you! Lend me some money just this once.

entries.english: both as bad as each other
entries.englishIdiom: six of one and half a dozen of the other
entries.use: The verdict on a quarrel or a couple's fight where neither side is innocent: sore wa dotchi mo dotchi da yo. Also for two equally poor choices. It refuses to take sides, unlike kata o motsu.

example.romaji: sore wa dotchi mo dotchi da yo.
example.ja: それはどっちもどっちだよ。
example.english: You're both as bad as each other.

examplePolite.romaji: kore wa, dotchi mo dotchi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: これは、どっちもどっちですね。
examplePolite.english: Honestly, they're both as bad as each other.

entries.english: lend your support, help (with something big)
entries.use: The serious ask for backing on a project, a cause or a hard situation: chikara o kashite hoshii (I need your help). Bigger than te o kasu (a quick hand); chikara ni naru is offering support yourself.

example.romaji: kono purojekuto, chikara kashite kurenai?
example.ja: このプロジェクト、力貸してくれない？
example.english: Would you help me out on this project?

examplePolite.romaji: kono purojekuto ni, zehi chikara o kashite itadakemasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: このプロジェクトに、ぜひ力を貸していただけませんか？
examplePolite.english: Would you be willing to help us with this project?

entries.notes: chie o kasu = help someone think something through.

entries.use: The rallying line for a team, class, family or workplace facing something hard, usually minna de chikara o awasete (all of us together). Heard in pep talks and speeches as much as in chat; te o kumu is two sides forming an alliance.

example.romaji: minna de chikara awasete ganbarou!
example.ja: みんなで力合わせて頑張ろう！
example.english: Let's all pull together!

examplePolite.romaji: minna de chikara o awasete ganbarimashou.
examplePolite.ja: みんなで力を合わせて頑張りましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's all pull together and do our best.

entries.english: not my problem, I couldn't care less
entries.literal: (it's) not a thing I know about
entries.use: A rough brush-off when someone's trouble lands on you: sonna no shitta kotcha nai (that's not my problem). Said in anger or bluster, more often by men; the milder version is kankei nai.

example.romaji: sonna no, ore no shitta kotcha nai yo.
example.ja: そんなの、俺の知ったこっちゃないよ。
example.english: That's not my problem.

entries.notes: Plain alternative: kankei nai (none of my business).

entries.english: who do you think you are
entries.englishIdiom: who do you think you are
entries.use: An angry retort to someone acting superior or bossy, said to their face or, more often, behind their back: ano hito, nanisama no tsumori? It's harsh, so keep it for real anger or venting.

example.romaji: ano hito, ittai nanisama no tsumori?
example.ja: あの人、いったい何様のつもり？
example.english: Who does she think she is?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito, ittai nanisama no tsumori na n deshou ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人、いったい何様のつもりなんでしょうね。
examplePolite.english: Who does she think she is?

entries.notes: Short form: nanisama? / nanisama da yo.

entries.use: About a shy child, a new colleague, a rescued pet or a guarded partner finally trusting you: yatto kokoro o hiraite kureta, or nakanaka kokoro o hirakanai. kyori o oku is the opposite move.

example.romaji: ano ko, yatto kokoro hiraite kureta.
example.ja: あの子、やっと心開いてくれた。
example.english: She's finally opened up to me.

examplePolite.romaji: ano ko, yatto kokoro o hiraite kureta n desu.
examplePolite.ja: あの子、やっと心を開いてくれたんです。
examplePolite.english: She's finally opened up to me.

entries.notes: Close: kokoro o yurusu / ki o yurusu (trust someone, let your guard down).

entries.english: keep your distance, take time apart
entries.use: Relationship talk: shibaraku kyori o okitai (I want some time apart), or stepping back from a draining friend or group. Softer than wakareru: it's a break, not a breakup.

example.romaji: shibaraku kyori oita hou ga ii yo.
example.ja: しばらく距離置いたほうがいいよ。
example.english: You two should take some time apart.

examplePolite.romaji: shibaraku kyori o oita hou ga ii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: しばらく距離を置いたほうがいいですよ。
examplePolite.english: You'd be better off taking some time apart.

entries.use: Almost always a softener before blunt words: ki o waruku shinaide (no offense, but...). The subject is the person who might feel hurt; ki ni sawaru is the remark that does the hurting.

example.romaji: ki o waruku shinaide kiite ne.
example.ja: 気を悪くしないで聞いてね。
example.english: Don't take this the wrong way, but hear me out.

examplePolite.romaji: ki o waruku shinaide kiite kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 気を悪くしないで聞いてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: Please don't take this the wrong way.

entries.english: try to get someone's attention (often romantic)
entries.use: Dating talk about playing for someone's interest: kare no ki o hikitakute (because I wanted his attention); also a child acting up to be noticed. It's the effort; ki ga aru is already being into someone, and myaku ga aru is them liking you back.

example.romaji: kare no ki o hikitakute, wazato sokkenaku shiteru no.
example.ja: 彼の気を引きたくて、わざとそっけなくしてるの。
example.english: I'm playing it cool on purpose to get his attention.

examplePolite.romaji: kare no ki o hikitakute, wazato sokkenaku shite iru n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の気を引きたくて、わざとそっけなくしているんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm playing it cool on purpose to get his attention.

entries.notes: Not hiku on its own, slang for being put off (sore wa hiku).

entries.politeJa: 足手まといになります
entries.english: be a burden, slow others down
entries.literal: become a tangle round hands and feet
entries.use: Mostly said about yourself when refusing help or staying behind: ashidematoi ni naritakunai (I don't want to slow you down); said to others it's harsh. Unlike ashi o hipparu (dragging a result down), it's being a burden just by being there.

example.romaji: ashidematoi ni naritakunai kara, saki itte.
example.ja: 足手まといになりたくないから、先行って。
example.english: I don't want to slow you down, go on ahead.

examplePolite.romaji: ashidematoi ni naritakunai node, saki ni itte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 足手まといになりたくないので、先に行ってください。
examplePolite.english: I don't want to slow you down, so please go ahead.

entries.english: cross the line; (of two people) sleep together
entries.use: Gossip about two people who've become lovers (ano futari, issen koeta rashii yo), or about going too far in a fight or a joke. The romantic sense is the one you'll hear most.

example.romaji: ano futari, mou issen koeta rashii yo.
example.ja: あの二人、もう一線越えたらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently those two have already slept together.

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari, mou issen o koeta rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人、もう一線を越えたらしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Apparently those two have already slept together.

entries.notes: issen o hiku = draw a line, keep a boundary.

entries.use: Most often in the apology ki ni sawattara gomen (sorry if that upset you), or about a grating manner (ano iikata ga ki ni sawaru). The subject is the remark, not the hurt person (that's ki o waruku suru); not ki ni naru (be on your mind).

example.romaji: nanka ki ni sawatta nara, gomen ne.
example.ja: なんか気に障ったなら、ごめんね。
example.english: Sorry if I said something that upset you.

examplePolite.romaji: nanika oki ni sawattara, moushiwake arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 何かお気に障ったら、申し訳ありません。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry if anything I said upset you.

entries.english: let it slide, go easy on someone
entries.literal: look at it by a generous measure
entries.use: Asking for or granting leniency over a small offence, usually kondo dake oome ni mite (just this once). A boss, parent or teacher does it; mizu ni nagasu is forgiving after a real fight.

example.romaji: kondo dake, oome ni mite yo.
example.ja: 今度だけ、大目に見てよ。
example.english: Just this once, let it slide.

examplePolite.romaji: kondo dake, oome ni mite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今度だけ、大目に見てください。
examplePolite.english: Just this once, please let it slide.

entries.literal: wash it away in the water
entries.use: Making up after a fight or a grudge, usually as mizu ni nagasou (let's put it behind us). Different from nakatta koto ni suru, which pretends it never happened rather than forgiving it. Not mizu o nagasu (flush, run the water) or mizu o sasu (put a damper on).

example.romaji: mou mukashi no koto da shi, mizu ni nagasou yo.
example.ja: もう昔のことだし、水に流そうよ。
example.english: It's all in the past, let's put it behind us.

examplePolite.romaji: mou mukashi no koto desu shi, mizu ni nagashimashou.
examplePolite.ja: もう昔のことですし、水に流しましょう。
examplePolite.english: It's all in the past, let's put it behind us.

entries.english: go to a lot of trouble (for someone)
entries.use: Mostly in thanks for effort made on your behalf: iroiro hone otte kurete arigatou, or hone o otte itadaite at work. Also literally breaking a bone (ashi no hone o otta); hone ga oreru is a job being hard work.

example.romaji: iroiro hone otte kurete, arigatou.
example.ja: いろいろ骨折ってくれて、ありがとう。
example.english: Thanks for going to all that trouble.

examplePolite.romaji: iroiro to hone o otte itadaite, arigatou gozaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: いろいろと骨を折っていただいて、ありがとうございました。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for going to so much trouble for us.

entries.notes: Noun: honeori (honeori zon = all that effort for nothing).

entries.use: Breaking off for good with family, an ex, a toxic friend or a gang, often oya to en o kitta or ano hito to wa mou en o kitta. Far stronger than kyori o oku (a break).

example.romaji: ano hito to wa mou en kitta kara.
example.ja: あの人とはもう縁切ったから。
example.english: I've cut ties with her.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito to wa, mou en o kirimashita.
examplePolite.ja: あの人とは、もう縁を切りました。
examplePolite.english: I've cut ties with her.

entries.notes: Also te o kiru (break off with a partner or associate).

entries.english: I owe you big, I'm really grateful
entries.use: A heartfelt, slightly old-school thank-you when someone bails you out, mostly men among friends: warui na, on ni kiru yo. kari ga aru describes the debt; this is the thanks you say on the spot.

example.romaji: warui na, on ni kiru yo.
example.ja: 悪いな、恩に着るよ。
example.english: Thanks, man. I owe you big.

examplePolite.romaji: hontou ni tasukarimashita. on ni kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 本当に助かりました。恩に着ます。
examplePolite.english: You really saved me. I owe you big.

entries.notes: on o kaesu = repay a kindness; onkisegamashii = making a big show of a favour.

entries.english: make an enemy of, get on someone's bad side
entries.use: A warning about someone powerful or vindictive: ano hito o teki ni mawasu to kowai yo. Also about taking on many at once (minna o teki ni mawashite mo); mikata ni tsukeru (win someone over) is the opposite.

example.romaji: ano hito o teki ni mawasu to kowai yo.
example.ja: あの人を敵に回すと怖いよ。
example.english: You don't want to get on her bad side.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito o teki ni mawasu to kowai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの人を敵に回すと怖いですよ。
examplePolite.english: You don't want to get on her bad side.

entries.literal: put the twist back in the strands
entries.use: Dating gossip about exes: motokare to yori modoshita (she got back with her ex). Only for couples; friends making up is nakanaori.

example.romaji: ano futari, mata yori modoshita rashii yo.
example.ja: あの二人、またより戻したらしいよ。
example.english: Apparently those two got back together again.

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari, mata yori o modoshita rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの二人、またよりを戻したらしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Apparently those two got back together again.

entries.notes: Noun in gossip: fukuen (getting back together).

entries.use: Confronting someone provocative, usually kenka utteru no? (are you looking for a fight?), half-joking among friends, rough with strangers. The other side is kenka o kau (take up the challenge).

example.romaji: nani sore, kenka utteru no?
example.ja: 何それ、喧嘩売ってるの？
example.english: What's that supposed to mean, you looking for a fight?

examplePolite.romaji: sore, kenka utteru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: それ、喧嘩売ってるんですか？
examplePolite.english: Are you trying to pick a fight with me?

entries.notes: Accepting: kenka o kau (sono kenka, katta = you're on).

entries.english: call it a night, wrap up (a party)
entries.use: How a party, drinking session or wedding gets ended, since owaru is avoided at celebrations: jaa, sorosoro ohiraki ni shiyou ka. When telling what happened: ohiraki ni natta (it broke up).

example.romaji: jaa, sorosoro ohiraki ni shiyou ka.
example.ja: じゃあ、そろそろお開きにしようか。
example.english: OK, shall we call it a night?

examplePolite.romaji: sore de wa, sorosoro ohiraki ni shitai to omoimasu.
examplePolite.ja: それでは、そろそろお開きにしたいと思います。
examplePolite.english: Well, I think it's about time we wrapped up.

entries.use: Stresses there's no connection at all, often bitterly: after a breakup, mou aka no tanin. Aka here means 'complete', not the colour.

example.romaji: wakaretara, mou aka no tanin da yo.
example.ja: 別れたら、もう赤の他人だよ。
example.english: Once you break up, you're total strangers.

examplePolite.romaji: wakaretara, mou aka no tanin desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 別れたら、もう赤の他人ですよ。
examplePolite.english: Once you break up, you're total strangers.

entries.notes: Plain alternative: tanin (outsider, someone not family).

entries.use: A work and family complaint about fixing what someone else messed up: mata ore ga ano hito no shirinugui ka yo. Often shirinugui o saserareru (get stuck cleaning up); ashi o hipparu is the one making the mess.

example.romaji: mata ore ga ano hito no shirinugui ka yo.
example.ja: また俺があの人の尻拭いかよ。
example.english: So I'm cleaning up his mess again?

examplePolite.romaji: mata watashi ga ano hito no shirinugui o suru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: また私があの人の尻拭いをするんですか？
examplePolite.english: So I'm cleaning up his mess again?

entries.use: Office and school talk about someone flattering the boss or teacher: buchou ni goma sutteru. The suru is 擂る (grind), so it's sutteru and surimasu, not shiteru or shimasu.

example.romaji: ano hito, itsumo buchou ni goma sutteru yo ne.
example.ja: あの人、いつも部長にごますってるよね。
example.english: He's always sucking up to the boss, isn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito, itsumo buchou ni goma suttemasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人、いつも部長にごますってますよね。
examplePolite.english: He's always sucking up to the boss, isn't he?

entries.notes: Noun: gomasuri (a suck-up).

entries.use: Smoothing things over with a sulking partner, child or grumpy boss, often as gokigen o toru. It's about soothing a mood; goma o suru is flattery to curry favour.

example.romaji: kanojo no kigen toru no, taihen na n da yo.
example.ja: 彼女の機嫌取るの、大変なんだよ。
example.english: Keeping my girlfriend happy is hard work.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo no kigen o toru no, taihen na n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女の機嫌を取るの、大変なんですよ。
examplePolite.english: Keeping my girlfriend happy is hard work.

entries.notes: Also gokigen o toru; noun gokigentori.

entries.english: be meant to be, have a connection
entries.use: Heard most in the negative to soften a breakup, rejection or failed job hunt: en ga nakatta n da yo (it just wasn't meant to be). In business it's the polite goodbye mata goen ga areba (if our paths cross again).

example.romaji: kanojo to wa en ga nakatta n da yo.
example.ja: 彼女とは縁がなかったんだよ。
example.english: It just wasn't meant to be with her.

examplePolite.romaji: kanojo to wa, en ga nakatta n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼女とは、縁がなかったんですよ。
examplePolite.english: It just wasn't meant to be with her.

entries.notes: On a chance meeting: kore mo nanika no en (this must be fate).

entries.use: Usually teasing or defensive, in the -teru form: mada ne ni motteru no? (still sore about that?). The opposite of mizu ni nagasu.

example.romaji: mada ano koto ne ni motteru no?
example.ja: まだあのこと根に持ってるの？
example.english: You're still holding a grudge about that?

examplePolite.romaji: mada ano koto o ne ni motte iru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: まだあのことを根に持っているんですか？
examplePolite.english: Are you still holding a grudge about that?

entries.use: Said on finding a mutual friend or bumping into someone unexpectedly, almost always with ne. Younger speakers also say sekai wa semai.

example.romaji: e, kare to shiriai na no? seken wa semai ne.
example.ja: え、彼と知り合いなの？世間は狭いね。
example.english: Wait, you know him? Small world.

examplePolite.romaji: e, kare to oshiriai na n desu ka? seken wa semai desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: え、彼とお知り合いなんですか？世間は狭いですね。
examplePolite.english: Oh, you know him? Small world.

entries.notes: Variant: sekai wa semai.

entries.english: put a damper on, spoil the mood
entries.use: Mostly the apology before bad news or an objection: mizu sasu you de warui kedo (sorry to be a downer, but). Also coming between a happy couple or friends (futari no naka ni mizu o sasu). Not mizu ni nagasu (forgive and forget).

example.romaji: mizu sasu you de warui kedo, sono hi ame rashii yo.
example.ja: 水差すようで悪いけど、その日雨らしいよ。
example.english: Sorry to be a downer, but it's supposed to rain that day.

examplePolite.romaji: mizu o sasu you de moushiwake nai n desu ga, sono hi wa ame rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 水を差すようで申し訳ないんですが、その日は雨らしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Sorry to be a downer, but it's supposed to rain that day.

entries.use: A staple of arguments and family fights, usually a complaint about unfair favouring: dotchi no kata motsu no? (whose side are you on?). Different from senaka o osu, which is encouraging someone to act.

example.romaji: nande itsumo ano ko no kata motsu no?
example.ja: なんでいつもあの子の肩持つの？
example.english: Why do you always take her side?

examplePolite.romaji: doushite itsumo ano hito no kata o motsu n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: どうしていつもあの人の肩を持つんですか？
examplePolite.english: Why do you always take her side?

entries.english: two-time, date two people at once
entries.use: Dating gossip and accusations, often passive: futamata kakerareteta (I was being two-timed). Mostly romance; it can also mean hedging between two options (two job offers).

example.romaji: kare ni futamata kakerareteta no.
example.ja: 彼に二股かけられてたの。
example.english: He was two-timing me.

examplePolite.romaji: kare ni futamata o kakerarete ita n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 彼に二股をかけられていたんです。
examplePolite.english: He was two-timing me.

entries.notes: Casual: futamata suru.

entries.english: just click with someone, get on well
entries.use: The same as ki ga au, said of two people who get on naturally, often with a hint of surprise: buchou to wa fushigi to uma ga au. Common in the negative too (dou mo uma ga awanai). Don't hear it as umai (tasty, skilled).

example.romaji: buchou to wa, fushigi to uma ga au n da.
example.ja: 部長とは、不思議と馬が合うんだ。
example.english: Weirdly, I really click with my boss.

examplePolite.romaji: buchou to wa, fushigi to uma ga au n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 部長とは、不思議と馬が合うんです。
examplePolite.english: Weirdly, I really click with my boss.

entries.notes: From riding: horse and rider in step.

entries.use: A complaint about being the last to know or shut out of a decision: nande ore dake kaya no soto na no? Heard at work, among friends and in families, often as kaya no soto ni sareta (got shut out).

example.romaji: nande ore dake kaya no soto na no?
example.ja: なんで俺だけ蚊帳の外なの？
example.english: Why am I the only one left out?

examplePolite.romaji: watashi dake kaya no soto datta n desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 私だけ蚊帳の外だったんですね。
examplePolite.english: So I was the only one left out of the loop.

entries.english: there's a chance (they like you back)
entries.use: Dating talk reading someone's signals, nearly always as myaku ari (promising) or myaku nashi (no chance): sore, myaku ari da yo. The literal 'there's a pulse' is medical; ki ga aru is someone actually being into you.

example.romaji: henji sugu kuru n desho? sore, myaku ari da yo.
example.ja: 返事すぐ来るんでしょ？それ、脈ありだよ。
example.english: He texts back right away? You've got a shot.

examplePolite.romaji: henji ga hayai nara, myaku ari desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 返事が早いなら、脈ありですよ。
examplePolite.english: If he replies fast, you've got a shot.

entries.notes: Usually myaku ari / myaku nashi.

entries.english: (negative) disapprove; play nice to please people
entries.use: Two everyday uses. The negative ii kao o shinai is parents or a boss not approving (oya ga ii kao shinai). The positive is being nice to keep people happy, often dare ni demo ii kao suru (a people-pleaser). Don't confuse it with kao ga ii (good-looking).

example.romaji: oya ga ii kao shinai n da yo ne, kare no koto.
example.ja: 親がいい顔しないんだよね、彼のこと。
example.english: My parents aren't too happy about him.

examplePolite.romaji: ryoushin ga, amari ii kao o shinai n desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 両親が、あまりいい顔をしないんですよね。
examplePolite.english: My parents aren't too happy about it.

entries.notes: A people-pleaser: dare ni demo ii kao suru hito (happou bijin).

entries.english: be bossed around by your wife
entries.literal: be laid under (someone's) bottom like a cushion
entries.use: Light teasing about a husband or boyfriend, almost always in the -teru form: okusan no shiri ni shikareteru. Rarely a real insult.

example.romaji: kare, kanzen ni okusan no shiri ni shikareteru yo ne.
example.ja: 彼、完全に奥さんの尻に敷かれてるよね。
example.english: He's totally under his wife's thumb.

examplePolite.romaji: kare, kanzen ni okusan no shiri ni shikaretemasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼、完全に奥さんの尻に敷かれてますよね。
examplePolite.english: He's totally under his wife's thumb.

entries.english: owe someone too much to stand up to them
entries.use: About a wife, older sibling, mentor or boss who's done so much for you that you can never argue back: ane ni wa atama ga agaranai. Always negative and said with fond resignation; shiri ni shikareru is being bossed around without the gratitude.

example.romaji: ane ni wa atama ga agaranai n da yo.
example.ja: 姉には頭が上がらないんだよ。
example.english: I owe my sister too much to ever argue with her.

examplePolite.romaji: ane ni wa, hontou ni atama ga agarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 姉には、本当に頭が上がりません。
examplePolite.english: I owe my sister so much, I can never argue with her.

entries.use: Mostly a complaint about someone always checking how a boss, parent or partner will react: joushi no kaoiro bakkari ukagatteru. Close to kuuki o yomu, but fixed on one person's mood and the fear of upsetting them.

example.romaji: ano hito, itsumo joushi no kaoiro bakkari ukagatteru.
example.ja: あの人、いつも上司の顔色ばっかりうかがってる。
example.english: He's always tiptoeing around the boss.

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito, itsumo joushi no kaoiro bakari ukagattemasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人、いつも上司の顔色ばかりうかがってますよね。
examplePolite.english: He's always tiptoeing around the boss, isn't he?

entries.notes: Literal kaoiro ga warui = look pale.

entries.use: Said before janken, a draw, a bet or a vote so the loser won't sulk: uramikko nashi ne. Also after the result, to keep things friendly.

example.romaji: janken de kimeyou. uramikko nashi ne.
example.ja: じゃんけんで決めよう。恨みっこなしね。
example.english: Let's settle it with rock-paper-scissors. No hard feelings.

examplePolite.romaji: dou natte mo, uramikko nashi desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: どうなっても、恨みっこなしですよ。
examplePolite.english: Whatever happens, no hard feelings.

entries.english: let someone save face, defer to them
entries.use: Going along with a senior, a host or whoever introduced you so they don't look bad: koko wa senpai no kao o tatete. Often the reason you accept something you'd rather refuse; kao o tsubusu is the opposite.

example.romaji: koko wa senpai no kao o tatete, damatte okou.
example.ja: ここは先輩の顔を立てて、黙っておこう。
example.english: Let's keep quiet and let our senior save face.

examplePolite.romaji: koko wa senpai no kao o tatete, damatte okimashou.
examplePolite.ja: ここは先輩の顔を立てて、黙っておきましょう。
examplePolite.english: Let's keep quiet and let our senior save face.

entries.use: Said to a friend, partner or relative who's being too polite or reserved with you: tanin gyougi da na (why so formal?). Often about keigo, over-thanking or refusing help; aka no tanin is an actual stranger.

example.romaji: keigo nante tanin gyougi da yo. futsuu ni hanashite.
example.ja: 敬語なんて他人行儀だよ。普通に話して。
example.english: Keigo feels so distant. Just talk normally.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna tanin gyougi na koto iwanaide kudasai yo.
examplePolite.ja: そんな他人行儀なこと言わないでくださいよ。
examplePolite.english: Don't be so formal with me.

entries.english: make someone (who vouched for you) look bad
entries.use: A warning to someone you introduced or recommended: ore no kao, tsubusanaide yo (don't embarrass me). Also the complaint ore no kao o tsubushita; kao o tateru is the opposite.

example.romaji: shoukai shita ore no kao, tsubusanaide yo.
example.ja: 紹介した俺の顔、潰さないでよ。
example.english: I introduced you, so don't make me look bad.

examplePolite.romaji: shoukai shita watashi no kao o tsubusanaide kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 紹介した私の顔を潰さないでくださいね。
examplePolite.english: I introduced you, so please don't make me look bad.

entries.notes: Stronger: kao ni doro o nuru (oya no kao ni doro o nuru = disgrace your parents).

entries.englishIdiom: birds of a feather flock together
entries.use: A wry comment when a group turns out to share the same quirk or vice: rui wa tomo o yobu tte yatsu da ne. Can be teasing or a dig.

example.romaji: ano guruupu, minna nonbee da ne. rui wa tomo o yobu tte yatsu da.
example.ja: あのグループ、みんな飲兵衛だね。類は友を呼ぶってやつだ。
example.english: That whole group are big drinkers. Birds of a feather.

examplePolite.romaji: ano guruupu, minna osake ga suki desu ne. rui wa tomo o yobu tte yatsu desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あのグループ、みんなお酒が好きですね。類は友を呼ぶってやつですね。
examplePolite.english: That whole group loves a drink. Birds of a feather.

entries.notes: Short form: ruitomo.

entries.use: The worry behind every soft refusal or bit of feedback, usually kado ga tatanai you ni (so there's no bad feeling) or sonna iikata shitara kado ga tatsu. It's the wording or act causing friction; ki ni sawaru is how the other person takes it.

example.romaji: sonna iikata shitara, kado ga tatsu yo.
example.ja: そんな言い方したら、角が立つよ。
example.english: Saying it like that will rub people the wrong way.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna iikata o shitara, kado ga tachimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: そんな言い方をしたら、角が立ちますよ。
examplePolite.english: Saying it like that will rub people the wrong way.

entries.notes: Opposite: maruku osamaru (be settled smoothly).

entries.romaji: kenka suru hodo naka ga ii
entries.ja: 喧嘩するほど仲がいい
entries.kana: けんかするほどなかがいい
entries.english: the more you fight, the closer you are
entries.literal: close to the point of fighting
entries.use: Said about a bickering couple, siblings or friends, half teasing: kenka suru hodo naka ga ii tte iu shi ne. Also a consolation after you've argued with someone you love.

example.romaji: mata kenka shiteru no? maa, kenka suru hodo naka ga ii tte iu shi ne.
example.ja: また喧嘩してるの？まあ、喧嘩するほど仲がいいって言うしね。
example.english: Fighting again? Well, they say the more you fight, the closer you are.

examplePolite.romaji: kenka suru hodo naka ga ii tte iimasu kara ne.
examplePolite.ja: 喧嘩するほど仲がいいって言いますからね。
examplePolite.english: They do say the more you fight, the closer you are.

entries.romaji: yoso wa yoso, uchi wa uchi
entries.ja: よそはよそ、うちはうち
entries.kana: よそはよそ、うちはうち
entries.english: other families do as they like; we do it our way
entries.literal: elsewhere is elsewhere, home is home
entries.use: Every parent's reply to 'but everyone else has one / is allowed': yoso wa yoso, uchi wa uchi. Also more widely, that other people's choices aren't yours to copy.

example.romaji: minna motteru tte? yoso wa yoso, uchi wa uchi desho.
example.ja: みんな持ってるって？よそはよそ、うちはうちでしょ。
example.english: Everyone has one? Other families can do what they like; this is our house.

examplePolite.romaji: yoso wa yoso, uchi wa uchi desu kara.
examplePolite.ja: よそはよそ、うちはうちですから。
examplePolite.english: Other places do things their way; we do ours.

entries.use: A playful comment when a friend or partner reads your mind: ishin denshin da ne. Said about couples, close friends or a well-tuned team.

example.romaji: sore iou to omotteta! ishin denshin da ne.
example.ja: それ言おうと思ってた！以心伝心だね。
example.english: I was just about to say that! You read my mind.

examplePolite.romaji: sore, ima iou to omotte imashita. ishin denshin desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: それ、今言おうと思っていました。以心伝心ですね。
examplePolite.english: I was just about to say that. You read my mind.

entries.politeJa: 言うまでもありません
entries.english: needless to say, it goes without saying; (X wa iu made mo naku) not to mention X
entries.literal: no need to go as far as saying it
entries.use: Comes before a point everyone already knows, as iu made mo nai kedo... (needless to say...), or as a reply: iu made mo nai desho (that goes without saying). Its most frequent form is iu made mo naku, which after a noun means 'not to mention': eigo wa iu made mo naku, chuugokugo mo perapera (she's fluent in Chinese, not to mention English). It sounds a little formal and is heard most in speeches and announcements; friends often just say mochiron.

example.romaji: iu made mo nai kedo, kore naisho ne.
example.ja: 言うまでもないけど、これ内緒ね。
example.english: Needless to say, this stays between us.

examplePolite.romaji: iu made mo arimasen ga, kore wa naisho de onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 言うまでもありませんが、これは内緒でお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Needless to say, please keep this to yourself.

entries.notes: Pattern: X made mo nai (no need even to X), as in miru made mo nai. Plain alternatives: mochiron, atarimae.

entries.use: A slightly more formal way to say you hear a word, name or rumour in passing: saikin yoku mimi ni suru (you hear it a lot lately), hajimete mimi ni shita (first I've heard of it). It's hearing by chance, not listening on purpose (that's kiku); news reaching you is mimi ni hairu.

example.romaji: sono hanashi, saikin yoku mimi ni suru yo ne.
example.ja: その話、最近よく耳にするよね。
example.english: You hear about that a lot lately, don't you?

examplePolite.romaji: sono hanashi, saikin yoku mimi ni shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: その話、最近よく耳にしますね。
examplePolite.english: You hear about that a lot these days.

entries.notes: Plain alternative: kiku (sono hanashi kiita).

entries.english: heed, give someone a hearing (mostly 'won't listen'); lean in so I can whisper
entries.use: Mostly negative, about ignoring advice or pleas: dare no iu koto ni mo mimi o kasanai (won't listen to anyone), ano hito no hanashi ni mimi o kasu na (don't listen to him). In casual talk, chotto mimi kashite means 'come here, let me whisper something'. Ordinary 'listen' is still kiku.

example.romaji: chotto mimi kashite.
example.ja: ちょっと耳貸して。
example.english: Come here, let me whisper something.

examplePolite.romaji: buchou, sukoshi wa genba no koe ni mo mimi o kashite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 部長、少しは現場の声にも耳を貸してください。
examplePolite.english: Please listen to the people on the ground for once.

entries.english: you've got some nerve, look who's talking
entries.use: A retort when someone says something cheeky, shameless or hypocritical: yoku iu yo, jibun datte... (you've got a nerve, when you...). Among friends it's often half-laughing. It's a different thing from plain yoku iu (people often say), which has no retort tone. Even as yoku iimasu ne it is a jab: say it to equals or about a third person, never to a boss.

example.romaji: yoku iu yo, jibun datte okureta kuse ni.
example.ja: よく言うよ、自分だって遅れたくせに。
example.english: Look who's talking. You were late too!

examplePolite.romaji: yoku iimasu ne. sochira datte okurete kita ja nai desu ka.
examplePolite.ja: よく言いますね。そちらだって遅れてきたじゃないですか。
examplePolite.english: That's rich. You were late too, weren't you?

entries.notes: Variant: yoku ieru ne (how can you even say that).

entries.english: butt in, put in one's two cents (in talk or matters that aren't yours)
entries.use: Butting into other people's conversation or business, heard as kuchi hasamanaide (stay out of this) or the polite preface kuchi o hasamu you desu ga (sorry to cut in). kuchi o dasu is close but stronger, actively meddling; cutting someone off mid-sentence is hanashi no koshi o oru, and kuchi ni dasu is just saying something out loud.

example.romaji: ima daiji na hanashi da kara, kuchi hasamanaide.
example.ja: 今大事な話だから、口挟まないで。
example.english: This is important, so don't butt in.

examplePolite.romaji: ima daiji na hanashi na node, kuchi o hasamanaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 今大事な話なので、口を挟まないでください。
examplePolite.english: We're discussing something important, so please don't interrupt.

entries.english: that's not what we agreed; that's a different matter
entries.use: The complaint when the terms or plan turn out different from what you were told: chotto, hanashi ga chigau ja nai (hey, that's not what you said). It also means 'that's a different matter': sore to kore to wa hanashi ga chigau (those are two different things), akaji ni naru nara hanashi ga chigau (if we'd lose money, that changes things). There it overlaps with hanashi wa betsu.

example.romaji: e, kyuuryou sagaru no? hanashi ga chigau yo.
example.ja: え、給料下がるの？話が違うよ。
example.english: What, my pay's going down? That's not what we agreed.

examplePolite.romaji: e, kyuuryou ga sagaru n desu ka? hanashi ga chigaimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: え、給料が下がるんですか？話が違いますよ。
examplePolite.english: My pay is going down? That's not what we agreed.

entries.use: Dismisses an offer, an excuse or someone's performance as too poor to even talk about: kono nedan ja hanashi ni naranai (at this price, forget it). Said of a person, ano hito ja hanashi ni naranai means there's no reasoning with them.

example.romaji: ichiman en? sore ja hanashi ni naranai yo.
example.ja: 一万円？それじゃ話にならないよ。
example.english: Ten thousand yen? That's not even worth discussing.

examplePolite.romaji: ichiman en desu ka? sore ja hanashi ni narimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: 一万円ですか？それじゃ話になりませんよ。
examplePolite.english: Ten thousand yen? That's out of the question.

entries.notes: Casual: hanashi ni nannai.

entries.use: A jab at someone who promises and never follows through: mata kuchi dake jan (all talk again). You'll also hear kuchi bakkari and kuchi dake no hito (someone who's all talk). kuchi dake is about not following through; the boasting itself is ooguchi o tataku.

example.romaji: ano hito, itsumo kuchi dake da yo ne.
example.ja: あの人、いつも口だけだよね。
example.english: He's always all talk, isn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: ano hito, itsumo kuchi dake desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: あの人、いつも口だけですよね。
examplePolite.english: He's always all talk, isn't he?

entries.notes: Variant: kuchi bakkari.

entries.use: The usual opener before a secret or a frank opinion: koko dake no hanashi, ... It quietly asks the listener not to spread it.

example.romaji: koko dake no hanashi, kare kekkon suru n da tte.
example.ja: ここだけの話、彼結婚するんだって。
example.english: Between you and me, I hear he's getting married.

examplePolite.romaji: koko dake no hanashi, kare, kekkon suru rashii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: ここだけの話、彼、結婚するらしいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Between you and me, apparently he's getting married.

entries.use: Follows a condition that changes your answer: X nara hanashi wa betsu da (if it's X, that changes things), typically when an offer gets better. hanashi ga chigau can say the same thing (X nara hanashi ga chigau), but its everyday use is the complaint that a deal was changed on you.

example.romaji: ogori nara hanashi wa betsu da yo.
example.ja: おごりなら話は別だよ。
example.english: If it's your treat, that's a different story.

examplePolite.romaji: kyuuryou ga agaru nara hanashi wa betsu desu kedo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 給料が上がるなら話は別ですけどね。
examplePolite.english: If the pay went up, that'd be a different story.

entries.use: Vouches for someone, or for yourself, as safe to trust with a secret: kare, kuchi ga katai kara daijoubu. The opposite is kuchi ga karui.

example.romaji: daijoubu, watashi kuchi katai kara.
example.ja: 大丈夫、私口堅いから。
example.english: Don't worry, I can keep a secret.

examplePolite.romaji: daijoubu desu, watashi, kuchi wa katai desu kara.
examplePolite.ja: 大丈夫です、私、口は堅いですから。
examplePolite.english: Don't worry, I know how to keep a secret.

entries.kana: たんとうちょくにゅう
entries.use: Announces that you're about to say or ask something directly: tantou chokunyuu ni iu to / kiku kedo... (to put it plainly / I'll just ask). It sounds a bit formal, so friends often say zubari instead.

example.romaji: tantou chokunyuu ni kiku kedo, kanojo iru?
example.ja: 単刀直入に聞くけど、彼女いる？
example.english: I'll just come out and ask: got a girlfriend?

examplePolite.romaji: tantou chokunyuu ni kikimasu kedo, kanojo wa imasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 単刀直入に聞きますけど、彼女はいますか？
examplePolite.english: I'll get straight to the point: do you have a girlfriend?

entries.notes: Casual alternative: zubari.

entries.use: Describes someone who talks bluntly or rudely, usually with a softener: kuchi wa warui kedo ii hito da yo. It's about how they speak, not bad breath (that's kuchi ga kusai).

example.romaji: kare, kuchi wa warui kedo ii yatsu da yo.
example.ja: 彼、口は悪いけどいいやつだよ。
example.english: He's got a sharp tongue, but he's a good guy.

examplePolite.romaji: kare, kuchi wa warui kedo ii hito desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 彼、口は悪いけどいい人ですよ。
examplePolite.english: He can be blunt, but he's a good person.

entries.use: Said the moment the person you were talking about walks in or calls: a, uwasa o sureba! People clip the full saying uwasa o sureba kage ga sasu (talk of someone and their shadow appears).

example.romaji: a, uwasa o sureba kita yo.
example.ja: あ、噂をすれば来たよ。
example.english: Oh, speak of the devil, here he comes.

examplePolite.romaji: a, uwasa o sureba kimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: あ、噂をすれば来ましたね。
examplePolite.english: Oh, speak of the devil, here he is.

entries.notes: Full saying: uwasa o sureba kage ga sasu.

entries.use: Mostly in the past, as an apology or excuse for blurting out a secret or a careless remark: tsui kuchi ga subetchatta (it just slipped out). Also heard as kuchi o suberaseru (let it slip).

example.romaji: gomen, tsui kuchi ga subetchatta.
example.ja: ごめん、つい口が滑っちゃった。
example.english: Sorry, it just slipped out.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, tsui kuchi ga suberimashita.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、つい口が滑りました。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry, it just slipped out.

entries.use: Mostly about age, height or weight, often as a joke: gosai saba yonderu desho (you're knocking five years off). It works in either direction, knocking years off or adding a few centimetres, and casual speech drops the o. The image is fishmongers counting mackerel in a hurry and getting the count conveniently wrong.

example.romaji: nijuu hassai? zettai saba yonderu desho.
example.ja: 二十八歳？絶対サバ読んでるでしょ。
example.english: Twenty-eight? You're definitely knocking a few years off.

examplePolite.romaji: jitsu wa, chotto saba yondemashita.
examplePolite.ja: 実は、ちょっとサバ読んでました。
examplePolite.english: Actually, I knocked a few years off.

entries.english: say out loud, put into words, mention
entries.literal: put it out into the mouth
entries.use: Saying aloud what you've been thinking or feeling, often in the negative about feelings kept inside: kuchi ni dasanai to tsutawaranai yo (if you don't say it, they won't know). Also mentioning a name or subject you shouldn't: sono namae, kuchi ni dasu na (don't mention that name). Only the particle separates it from kuchi o dasu (to meddle); kuchi ni suru is a slightly more formal near-synonym.

example.romaji: omotteru dake ja dame, kuchi ni dasanai to.
example.ja: 思ってるだけじゃダメ、口に出さないと。
example.english: Just thinking it isn't enough. You have to say it.

examplePolite.romaji: omotteru dake ja dame desu yo, kuchi ni dasanai to.
examplePolite.ja: 思ってるだけじゃダメですよ、口に出さないと。
examplePolite.english: Just thinking it won't do. You have to say it.

entries.english: that makes it easy, that saves explaining
entries.use: Said when the other person already knows or agrees, so you can skip the explaining: sore nara hanashi ga hayai (well, that makes it easy). Said of a person, it means they catch on fast. It has nothing to do with talking fast, which is hayakuchi.

example.romaji: shitteru nara hanashi ga hayai ne.
example.ja: 知ってるなら話が早いね。
example.english: If you already know, that makes it easy.

examplePolite.romaji: gozonji nara hanashi ga hayai desu.
examplePolite.ja: ご存じなら話が早いです。
examplePolite.english: If you already know, that makes things easier.

entries.notes: Also: hanashi wa hayai.

entries.literal: a callus forms on your ears
entries.use: The tired reply to advice or a story you've heard over and over, usually as mimi ni tako ga dekiru hodo kiita. The tako is a callus, not an octopus, though people joke about it. kuchi o suppaku shite iu is the same thing from the speaker's side.

example.romaji: sono hanashi, mimi ni tako ga dekiru hodo kiita yo.
example.ja: その話、耳にタコができるほど聞いたよ。
example.english: I've heard that one a million times.

examplePolite.romaji: sono hanashi, mimi ni tako ga dekiru hodo kikimashita yo.
examplePolite.ja: その話、耳にタコができるほど聞きましたよ。
examplePolite.english: I've heard that story more times than I can count.

entries.notes: Slangy short form: mimitako (mimitako da yo).

entries.politeJa: 人のことは言えません
entries.english: I'm not one to talk, I'm no better myself
entries.use: Softens your own complaint by admitting you do the same thing: watashi mo hito no koto ienai kedo... Turned on someone else, hito no koto ieru? is the jab 'are you really one to talk?'

example.romaji: maa, watashi mo hito no koto ienai kedo ne.
example.ja: まあ、私も人のこと言えないけどね。
example.english: Well, I'm not one to talk.

examplePolite.romaji: maa, watashi mo hito no koto wa iemasen kedo ne.
examplePolite.ja: まあ、私も人のことは言えませんけどね。
examplePolite.english: Well, I'm hardly one to talk.

entries.literal: heap up the story (like food on a plate)
entries.use: Modern casual way to say someone is puffing up a story to make it funnier or more impressive: sore, motteru desho (you're exaggerating). Moru alone is enough, and morisugi (way overdone) also covers heavy makeup or edited photos.

example.romaji: sore, zettai hanashi motteru desho.
example.ja: それ、絶対話盛ってるでしょ。
example.english: You're totally exaggerating that.

examplePolite.romaji: sore, zettai hanashi mottemasu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: それ、絶対話盛ってますよね。
examplePolite.english: You're definitely exaggerating that, right?

entries.notes: Plain alternative: oogesa (exaggerated).

entries.literal: it's not as if I didn't say it
entries.use: Said when things go wrong after someone ignored your warning: hora, iwan kotcha nai (see, I told you). It's a contraction of iwanai koto ja nai and sounds a bit parental. Friends also say dakara itta desho.

example.romaji: hora, iwan kotcha nai. nomisugi da yo.
example.ja: ほら、言わんこっちゃない。飲みすぎだよ。
example.english: See, I told you so. You drank too much.

entries.notes: Everyday alternative: dakara itta desho.

entries.use: A warning that someone blabs, so don't tell them anything: ano hito, kuchi ga karui kara ki o tsukete. Also kuchi no karui hito (a blabbermouth). The opposite of kuchi ga katai.

example.romaji: kare ni wa iwanaide, kuchi karui kara.
example.ja: 彼には言わないで、口軽いから。
example.english: Don't tell him. He's got a big mouth.

examplePolite.romaji: kare ni wa iwanaide kudasai, kuchi ga karui node.
examplePolite.ja: 彼には言わないでください、口が軽いので。
examplePolite.english: Please don't tell him. He can't keep a secret.

entries.english: make sure by telling someone again, stress, remind firmly
entries.use: Saying something again to make sure the other person has really understood or will really do it: ichiou nen oshitoku kedo... (just to be sure...). kugi o sasu is the stronger move, a warning not to do something.

example.romaji: ichiou nen oshitoku kedo, ashita juuji da yo.
example.ja: 一応念押しとくけど、明日十時だよ。
example.english: Just to be sure: it's ten o'clock tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ichiou nen o oshite okimasu ga, ashita juuji desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 一応念を押しておきますが、明日十時ですよ。
examplePolite.english: Just to make sure, it's ten o'clock tomorrow.

entries.notes: Related: nen no tame (just in case).

entries.use: Calls a rumour, an excuse or a claim totally untrue: sore, makka na uso da yo. The 'bright red' just means total and obvious.

example.romaji: ano uwasa? makka na uso da yo.
example.ja: あの噂？真っ赤な嘘だよ。
example.english: That rumour? It's a complete lie.

examplePolite.romaji: ano uwasa desu ka? makka na uso desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: あの噂ですか？真っ赤な嘘ですよ。
examplePolite.english: That rumour? It's an outright lie.

entries.notes: Plain alternatives: oouso, zenbu uso.

entries.politeJa: オブラートに包みます
entries.literal: wrap it in edible starch film
entries.use: About softening a blunt message, often as a request: mou chotto oburaato ni tsutsunde (put it more gently). The negative oburaato ni tsutsumazu ni iu means saying it straight out. Oburaato is the thin film once used to swallow bitter medicine.

example.romaji: mou chotto oburaato ni tsutsunde yo.
example.ja: もうちょっとオブラートに包んでよ。
example.english: Could you put it a bit more gently?

examplePolite.romaji: mou chotto oburaato ni tsutsunde moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: もうちょっとオブラートに包んでもらえますか？
examplePolite.english: Could you phrase that a little more gently?

entries.english: a white lie is sometimes needed
entries.literal: a lie is also an expedient
entries.use: Justifies a kind or convenient fib, such as telling a nervous friend they'll be fine: maa, uso mo houben da yo. Houben is a Buddhist word for a means to an end.

example.romaji: maa, uso mo houben tte iu shi.
example.ja: まあ、嘘も方便って言うし。
example.english: Well, sometimes a white lie is for the best.

examplePolite.romaji: maa, uso mo houben tte iimasu shi ne.
examplePolite.ja: まあ、嘘も方便って言いますしね。
examplePolite.english: Well, they do say a white lie can be necessary.

entries.use: Warning someone ahead of time not to do something, like telling, being late or overspending. It's often heard in the passive, kugi o sasareta (I was warned). nen o osu only double-checks; kugi o sasu is a warning.

example.romaji: dare ni mo iu na tte, kugi sasareta.
example.ja: 誰にも言うなって、釘刺された。
example.english: I got warned not to tell anyone.

examplePolite.romaji: dare ni mo iu na tte, kugi o sasaremashita.
examplePolite.ja: 誰にも言うなって、釘を刺されました。
examplePolite.english: I was told in no uncertain terms not to tell anyone.

entries.english: always says one thing too many
entries.use: A complaint about someone who can't resist adding one needless, annoying remark: itsumo hitokoto ooi n da yo. People say it about partners, bosses and parents, and about themselves when they regret a remark. The remark itself is yokei na hitokoto.

example.romaji: kare, itsumo hitokoto ooi n da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼、いつも一言多いんだよね。
example.english: He always has to add one comment too many.

examplePolite.romaji: kare, itsumo hitokoto ooi n desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼、いつも一言多いんですよね。
examplePolite.english: He always says one thing too many.

entries.notes: The remark itself: yokei na hitokoto.

entries.polite: mi mo futa mo nai desu
entries.english: brutally blunt, put so baldly there's nothing left to say
entries.use: A reaction to a remark so blunt or bleak that it kills the conversation, usually sore o itcha mi mo futa mo nai (if you say that, there's nothing left to talk about). Typical triggers are harsh truths like 'it all comes down to money'. Also mi mo futa mo nai iikata (a brutally blunt way of putting it).

example.romaji: sore o itcha, mi mo futa mo nai yo.
example.ja: それを言っちゃ、身も蓋もないよ。
example.english: Well, if you put it that bluntly, there's nothing left to say.

examplePolite.romaji: sore o itcha, mi mo futa mo nai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: それを言っちゃ、身も蓋もないですよ。
examplePolite.english: Putting it that way leaves nothing to discuss.

entries.english: ignore one's own faults while criticising others
entries.englishIdiom: the pot calling the kettle black
entries.use: Almost always jibun no koto wa tana ni agete..., calling out someone who criticises others for what they do themselves. It's also an admission: jibun no koto wa tana ni agete iu kedo (I know I'm no better, but...). Not to be confused with tanaage ni suru (shelve a plan or problem).

example.romaji: jibun no koto wa tana ni agete, hito no monku bakkari.
example.ja: 自分のことは棚に上げて、人の文句ばっかり。
example.english: He ignores his own faults and just complains about everyone else.

examplePolite.romaji: buchou tte, jibun no koto wa tana ni agete, hito no monku bakari desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 部長って、自分のことは棚に上げて、人の文句ばかりですよね。
examplePolite.english: The boss ignores his own faults and just complains about everyone else, doesn't he?

entries.ja: 口を酸っぱくして言う
entries.kana: くちをすっぱくしていう
entries.politeJa: 口を酸っぱくして言います
entries.literal: make one's mouth sour saying it
entries.englishIdiom: till I'm blue in the face
entries.use: A parent's or teacher's exasperation at a warning repeated many times, usually in the past: kuchi o suppaku shite itta desho. mimi ni tako ga dekiru is the same thing from the listener's side.

example.romaji: are hodo kuchi o suppaku shite itta noni.
example.ja: あれほど口を酸っぱくして言ったのに。
example.english: And I told you over and over!

examplePolite.romaji: are hodo kuchi o suppaku shite iimashita yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: あれほど口を酸っぱくして言いましたよね。
examplePolite.english: I told you again and again, didn't I?

entries.literal: not even a 'guu' sound comes out
entries.use: Admitting that someone's point is so right you can't argue back: seiron sugite guu no ne mo denai. Also said about someone else who lost an argument: kare, guu no ne mo denakatta.

example.romaji: sou iwaretara, guu no ne mo denai yo.
example.ja: そう言われたら、ぐうの音も出ないよ。
example.english: When you put it like that, I've got nothing.

examplePolite.romaji: sou iwaretara, guu no ne mo demasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: そう言われたら、ぐうの音も出ませんね。
examplePolite.english: Put like that, I can't argue.

entries.use: Goes with what you say, or can't say, directly to the person, usually in the negative: men to mukatte wa ienai. It's about complaints, thanks or confessions, not just meeting in person (that's chokusetsu au).

example.romaji: sonna koto, men to mukatte ienai yo.
example.ja: そんなこと、面と向かって言えないよ。
example.english: I can't say that to her face.

examplePolite.romaji: sonna koto, men to mukatte iemasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: そんなこと、面と向かって言えませんよ。
examplePolite.english: I couldn't say that to her face.

entries.english: that's my line; I should be the one saying that
entries.use: Throws someone's complaint or accusation straight back at them: sore wa kotchi no serifu da yo. You hear it in arguments and teasing, for example after 'you're late' or 'you're annoying'.

example.romaji: osoi tte, sore kotchi no serifu da yo.
example.ja: 遅いって、それこっちのセリフだよ。
example.english: 'You're late'? That's my line!

examplePolite.romaji: osoi tte, sore wa kotchi no serifu desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 遅いって、それはこっちのセリフですよ。
examplePolite.english: 'Late'? I should be the one saying that.

entries.notes: Formal: kochira no serifu desu.

entries.literal: say it that way and they say it this way
entries.use: An exasperated complaint about someone who argues back to everything, typically a parent about a child: hontou ni aa ieba kou iu n da kara. It's said about others, never about yourself.

example.romaji: mou, aa ieba kou iu n da kara.
example.ja: もう、ああ言えばこう言うんだから。
example.english: Honestly, you've got an answer for everything.

examplePolite.romaji: uchi no ko, hontou ni aa ieba kou iu n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: うちの子、本当にああ言えばこう言うんですよ。
examplePolite.english: My kid has an answer for everything.

entries.literal: split the belly open and talk
entries.use: An invitation to drop the politeness and say what you really think, usually as hara watte hanasou (let's talk honestly) between friends, partners or colleagues after some friction. The hara (belly) is where your true intentions are kept.

example.romaji: ikkai, hara o watte hanasou yo.
example.ja: 一回、腹を割って話そうよ。
example.english: Let's have a proper heart-to-heart.

examplePolite.romaji: ichido, hara o watte hanashimasen ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一度、腹を割って話しませんか？
examplePolite.english: Why don't we talk frankly, just this once?

entries.notes: Casual speech drops the o: hara watte hanasou.

entries.english: settle it by talking to someone, sort it out with them
entries.use: Going to someone, often the other side or the person in charge, and settling a problem or getting their OK by talking: ore ga hanashi tsukete kuru (I'll go sort it out with them). Crime dramas give it a hint of muscle, but everyday use is just arranging things.

example.romaji: ooya-san ni wa watashi ga hanashi tsuketoku ne.
example.ja: 大家さんには私が話つけとくね。
example.english: I'll sort it out with the landlord.

examplePolite.romaji: ooya-san ni wa watashi kara hanashi o tsukete okimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 大家さんには私から話をつけておきますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll get it settled with the landlord myself.

entries.notes: Once settled: hanashi ga tsuita (it's been sorted out).

entries.english: reach someone's ears, get word of
entries.use: News or a rumour reaching someone, often someone it shouldn't: buchou no mimi ni haittara yabai (if this gets to the boss, we're in trouble). Unlike mimi ni suru, the news is the subject; you just end up knowing. In the negative it can also mean you can't take in what's said: hanashi ga zenzen mimi ni hairanai.

example.romaji: sono uwasa, mou mimi ni haitteru yo.
example.ja: その噂、もう耳に入ってるよ。
example.english: That rumour's already reached me.

examplePolite.romaji: sono ken wa mou buchou no mimi ni haitte imasu.
examplePolite.ja: その件はもう部長の耳に入っています。
examplePolite.english: The manager has already heard about that.

entries.english: just a figure of speech, not meant literally
entries.use: The standard backpedal when someone takes your words too literally or too hard: ima no wa kotoba no aya da yo (that was just a way of putting it). Aya is the pattern woven into cloth.

example.romaji: gomen, ima no wa kotoba no aya da yo.
example.ja: ごめん、今のは言葉のあやだよ。
example.english: Sorry, that was just a figure of speech.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, ima no wa kotoba no aya desu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、今のは言葉のあやです。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I didn't mean that literally.

entries.english: don't say such ominous things, don't jinx it
entries.use: The quick rebuke when someone mentions death, illness, an accident or failure, even as a joke: engi demo nai koto iwanaide (don't say things like that). Engi is luck or omen, as in engi ga ii / engi ga warui.

example.romaji: chotto, engi demo nai koto iwanaide yo.
example.ja: ちょっと、縁起でもないこと言わないでよ。
example.english: Hey, bite your tongue! Don't say things like that.

examplePolite.romaji: engi demo nai koto iwanaide kudasai yo.
examplePolite.ja: 縁起でもないこと言わないでくださいよ。
examplePolite.english: Please don't say such ominous things.

entries.english: play dumb, pretend not to know
entries.use: Accusing someone of pretending not to know what you mean when they clearly do: shira kitte mo muda da yo (no use playing dumb). Mostly said to someone else, as shira o kiru na or shira kiranaide. Finally telling under pressure is the opposite, kuchi o waru.

example.romaji: shira kitte mo muda da yo, miteta n da kara.
example.ja: しら切っても無駄だよ、見てたんだから。
example.english: No use playing dumb, I saw you.

examplePolite.romaji: shira o kitte mo muda desu yo, mite ita n desu kara.
examplePolite.ja: しらを切っても無駄ですよ、見ていたんですから。
examplePolite.english: There's no point pretending, I saw everything.

entries.notes: Single-word alternative: shirabakkureru.

entries.english: can't fill the silence, run out of things to say
entries.literal: the pause can't be held up
entries.use: Said of a silence you can't fill: on a first date, in a lift with your boss, at a table where nobody talks. Usually about yourself or a situation, as futarikiri da to ma ga motanai (just the two of us, I run out of things to say). Also about killing time: sumaho ga nai to ma ga motanai.

example.romaji: futarikiri da to ma ga motanai n da yo ne.
example.ja: 二人きりだと間が持たないんだよね。
example.english: When it's just the two of us, I run out of things to say.

examplePolite.romaji: futarikiri da to ma ga motanai n desu yo ne.
examplePolite.ja: 二人きりだと間が持たないんですよね。
examplePolite.english: When it's just the two of us, I never know how to fill the silence.

entries.english: talk big, brag about what you'll do
entries.use: Bragging about what you can or will do, usually as a put-down or a warning: ooguchi tataku na (stop talking big). It's about the boast itself; kuchi dake is about never following through.

example.romaji: ooguchi tataku no wa katte kara ni shite.
example.ja: 大口叩くのは勝ってからにして。
example.english: Save the big talk for after you win.

examplePolite.romaji: ooguchi o tataku no wa katte kara ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 大口を叩くのは勝ってからにしてください。
examplePolite.english: Please save the big talk until you've actually won.

entries.notes: Casual variant: dekai kuchi o tataku.

entries.english: you've got some nerve (a sarcastic warning)
entries.use: A sarcastic warning to someone who has just done or said something bold or cheeky, half-joking among friends or mock-threatening from a senior. Unlike yoku iu yo, which calls out hypocrisy, it's about daring to do something.

example.romaji: watashi no purin tabeta no? ii dokyou shiteru ja nai.
example.ja: 私のプリン食べたの？いい度胸してるじゃない。
example.english: You ate my pudding? You've got some nerve.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi no purin, tabemashita? ii dokyou shitemasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 私のプリン、食べました？いい度胸してますね。
examplePolite.english: You ate my pudding? You've got some nerve.

entries.notes: Also: ii dokyou da ne.

entries.kana: はかばまでもっていく
entries.politeJa: 墓場まで持っていきます
entries.english: keep a secret to the grave
entries.literal: carry it as far as the graveyard
entries.use: Promising never to tell anyone, as a solemn vow or half-jokingly about something embarrassing: kono koto wa hakaba made motte iku (I'm taking this to the grave).

example.romaji: kono hanashi wa hakaba made motte iku yo.
example.ja: この話は墓場まで持っていくよ。
example.english: I'm taking this one to the grave.

examplePolite.romaji: kono hanashi wa hakaba made motte ikimasu yo.
examplePolite.ja: この話は墓場まで持っていきますよ。
examplePolite.english: I'll take this one to the grave.

entries.notes: Also: haka made motte iku.

entries.english: happen to hear, catch wind of
entries.literal: tuck it into a little ear
entries.use: Almost always in the past as a gossip opener: komimi ni hasanda n da kedo... (I happened to hear that...). It signals you heard it in passing and aren't sure it's true, which is softer than saying who told you.

example.romaji: komimi ni hasanda n da kedo, tanaka-san yameru no?
example.ja: 小耳に挟んだんだけど、田中さん辞めるの？
example.english: I happened to hear something. Is Tanaka quitting?

examplePolite.romaji: komimi ni hasanda n desu kedo, tanaka-san, yamerareru n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 小耳に挟んだんですけど、田中さん、辞められるんですか？
examplePolite.english: I happened to hear something. Is Ms Tanaka leaving?

entries.romaji: kokoro ni mo nai koto o iu
entries.polite: kokoro ni mo nai koto o iimasu
entries.ja: 心にもないことを言う
entries.kana: こころにもないことをいう
entries.politeJa: 心にもないことを言います
entries.literal: say things that aren't even in your heart
entries.use: Mostly in apologies after a fight: kokoro ni mo nai koto itchatta (I said things I didn't mean). The phrase kokoro ni mo nai also goes with flattery you don't mean: kokoro ni mo nai oseji.

example.romaji: tsui katto natte, kokoro ni mo nai koto itchatta.
example.ja: ついカッとなって、心にもないこと言っちゃった。
example.english: I lost my temper and said things I didn't mean.

examplePolite.romaji: tsui katto natte, kokoro ni mo nai koto o itte shimaimashita.
examplePolite.ja: ついカッとなって、心にもないことを言ってしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I lost my temper and said something I didn't mean.

entries.english: hit a sore spot, say exactly the wrong thing
entries.use: Modern casual talk for accidentally bringing up the one topic that upsets someone, like an ex, their weight or their exam results: a, jirai funda (oops, touched a nerve). A person's jirai is their sore subject.

example.romaji: a, ima jirai funda kamo.
example.ja: あ、今地雷踏んだかも。
example.english: Oops, I think I just touched a nerve.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, jirai o funde shimatta mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、地雷を踏んでしまったみたいです。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, it seems I touched a sore spot.

entries.english: I'm not following, where is this going?
entries.use: Said when you can't work out what someone is getting at or what it has to do with you: gomen, hanashi ga mienai n da kedo (sorry, I'm not following). It's about the point, not the words; not understanding the words is imi ga wakaranai.

example.romaji: gomen, hanashi ga mienai n da kedo.
example.ja: ごめん、話が見えないんだけど。
example.english: Sorry, I'm not following.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto hanashi ga mienai n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと話が見えないんですが。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I'm not quite following.

entries.use: Mostly negative, about someone who won't say what they know: nakanaka kuchi o waranai (just won't spill). Crime dramas use it for suspects; in daily life it's said jokingly about friends hiding a crush or kids hiding mischief. Letting something slip by accident is kuchi ga suberu.

example.romaji: kanojo, nakanaka kuchi o waranai n da yo ne.
example.ja: 彼女、なかなか口を割らないんだよね。
example.english: She just won't spill.

examplePolite.romaji: musuko ga nakanaka kuchi o waranai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 息子がなかなか口を割らないんです。
examplePolite.english: My son just won't own up.

entries.use: Going along with what someone says so as not to spoil the mood or blow a cover: tekitou ni hanashi awaseteta (I was just nodding along), or as a request: hanashi awasete ne (back me up, OK?). Really getting on in conversation is hanashi ga au.

example.romaji: kare no mae de wa, hanashi awasete ne.
example.ja: 彼の前では、話合わせてね。
example.english: In front of him, just play along, OK?

examplePolite.romaji: kare no mae de wa, hanashi o awasete kudasai ne.
examplePolite.ja: 彼の前では、話を合わせてくださいね。
examplePolite.english: When he's around, please play along.

entries.use: A good-humoured concession when someone outwits you with a clever reply or trick: kore wa ippon torareta na (well, you got me there). It's a fixed passive past; the ippon is a winning point in kendo or judo.

example.romaji: naruhodo ne, kore wa ippon torareta.
example.ja: なるほどね、これは一本取られた。
example.english: Ha, fair enough. You got me there.

examplePolite.romaji: naruhodo, kore wa ippon toraremashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: なるほど、これは一本取られましたね。
examplePolite.english: I see. You've got me there.

entries.english: it's all in how you put it
entries.literal: things depend on the way of saying
entries.use: A wry comment when someone dresses up something bad in nice words, or a reminder that the same thing can be said kindly or harshly: koseiteki tte, mono wa iiyou da ne ('unique'? nice way to put it). Also mono mo iiyou.

example.romaji: koseiteki tte, mono wa iiyou da ne.
example.ja: 個性的って、物は言いようだね。
example.english: 'Unique'? That's one way to put it.

examplePolite.romaji: koseiteki tte, mono wa iiyou desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 個性的って、物は言いようですね。
examplePolite.english: 'Unique'? That's a nice way of putting it.

entries.notes: Full saying: mono mo iiyou de kado ga tatsu (how you say it decides whether it offends).

entries.politeJa: バカなこと言わないでください
entries.english: don't be silly, don't talk nonsense
entries.use: Brushes off a ridiculous idea, or reassures someone who is putting themselves down: baka iwanaide, sonna wake nai desho (don't be silly, of course not). The rougher, mostly male form is baka iu na. In polite speech it becomes baka na koto iwanaide kudasai, which is still quite direct.

example.romaji: baka iwanaide, sonna wake nai desho.
example.ja: バカ言わないで、そんなわけないでしょ。
example.english: Don't be silly, of course not.

examplePolite.romaji: baka na koto iwanaide kudasai yo, sonna wake nai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: バカなこと言わないでくださいよ、そんなわけないですよ。
examplePolite.english: Don't be silly, that's not true at all.

entries.notes: Rougher: baka iu na; baka ie (yeah, right).

entries.english: interrupt and derail what someone is saying
entries.literal: break the waist of the talk
entries.use: Cutting in so the speaker loses their thread, as a complaint (hanashi no koshi oranaide) or an apology (hanashi no koshi o otte gomen). kuchi o hasamu is chiming in; this is derailing what someone was in the middle of saying.

example.romaji: chotto, hanashi no koshi oranaide yo.
example.ja: ちょっと、話の腰折らないでよ。
example.english: Hey, don't cut me off.

examplePolite.romaji: hanashi no koshi o otte sumimasen ga, hitotsu dake ii desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 話の腰を折ってすみませんが、一つだけいいですか？
examplePolite.english: Sorry to interrupt, but may I add just one thing?

entries.literal: stick a bad omen on it
entries.use: Criticising or nitpicking something, often unfairly or out of spite: nan ni demo kechi tsukeru (finds fault with everything). The kechi here is an old word for a bad omen, not kechi (stingy).

example.romaji: hito no ryouri ni kechi tsukenaide yo.
example.ja: 人の料理にケチつけないでよ。
example.english: Don't knock my cooking.

examplePolite.romaji: hito no ryouri ni kechi o tsukenaide kudasai yo.
examplePolite.ja: 人の料理にケチをつけないでくださいよ。
