consistency.notes:
I dropped only one entry. ma-ga-sasu and ma-ga-sashita were the same idiom (魔が差す), so the list goes from 422 to 421. The user wants more sets, so I kept every other entry: nothing else was a real duplicate, and nothing is in the collocation list.

COLLOCATION OVERLAP: no idiom headword matches a collocation-list item. Two idioms build on a literal set that is in that list, and both stay:
- kata no chikara o nuku is the figurative "stop trying so hard". The collocation entry for chikara o nuku names this sense itself.
- kokoro no junbi ga dekiru ("be emotionally ready") extends junbi ga dekiru. It is borderline literal, but it is its own common set phrase.

Fifteen idioms here were cut from the collocation list (ki ga au, me o tsuburu, kuse ni naru, me o samasu and others). Those are verdicts on cut items, not list items, so they belong here.

The versatility items ki ni naru, ki ni suru, ki ga suru and ki o tsukeru are not repeated. sono ki ni naru and ii ki ni naru are separate idioms. The versatility list spells nandemo and dotchi/kotchi the same way the idioms do (nani ga nandemo, dotchi mo dotchi, kotchi no serifu).

KEPT, ON PURPOSE:
- me-o-hanasu and me-ga-hanasenai (attention-2). The second is the "can't" form of the first (261 vs 19 hits), but they sit in the same block and are taught as a pair. If you want one entry per idiom, drop me-ga-hanasenai.
- Near-synonyms stay as separate idioms: jigou jitoku / mi kara deta sabi, ha ga tatanai / tachiuchi dekinai, omoi mo yoranai / yume ni mo omowanai, kuchi o dasu / kuchi o hasamu.

SPELLING: no fixes needed. The headwords follow the rules:
- -te iru, -te aru, -te kuru and -te iku are written as separate words (te ga konde iru, kao ni kaite aru, tsuke ga mawatte kuru), which matches how the collocation list writes them.
- Four-character compounds are split 2+2 (isseki nichou, chuuto hanpa, tanin gyougi).
- Fused words are written joined (ashidematoi, inochibiroi, damemoto).
- Copula and particles are separate (nani ga nan da ka, engi demo nai).
- Fixed said-forms are kept as said: ki ga kuruisou, yume ni mo omowanakatta, ma ga sashita, haraguroi.

CONTRAST GROUPS:
- "kuchi" had only one member (kuchi-ga-umai), so it is now null.
- "me-ga-nai" was a group of one that clearly meant to pair with me ga nai. Now me ga nai ("crazy about") and miru me ga nai ("poor judge") share it, since a listener can mix them up.
- "amaku-oome" was named for oome ni miru but did not include it. It now does, set against amaku miru.
- Form pairs now grouped, like the existing te-ni-ireru-hairu: ki ni kakeru / ki ni kakaru, hone o oru / hone ga oreru, iji o haru / mie o haru (new group o-haru), mono wa iiyou / mono wa kangaeyou (new group mono-wa-you).
- Natural pairs that had no group partner: atama ga okashii joins crazy (with dou ka shiteru), kao ni deru joins obvious (with kao ni kaite aru), ki ga kiku joins considerate (with ki o kubaru), ki ni kuwanai joins taking-offense (with ki ni sawaru), and rui wa tomo o yobu joins alike (with nita mono doushi).
- mendoumi ga ii now pairs with sewa ga yakeru in looking-after (one looks after, the other needs it), so that group keeps two members after ki ni kakeru moves.

COMMONNESS (not in this pass's scope, just noting): rui wa tomo o yobu has 1 hit across all its forms (類は友 / 類友). It is the weakest-evidenced entry left on the list.

stages.name: Stage 1
stages.summary: Say you've had enough or you're angry, ask for or offer help, describe people as clever, selfish or kind, and react to good luck and bad times.

stages.name: Stage 2
stages.summary: Say when you feel better or aren't in the mood, judge people by their skill and how they talk, point out hypocrisy, and talk about burdens, being busy and what catches your eye.

stages.name: Stage 3
stages.summary: Vent spite and frustration, describe stubborn or touchy people, let things go, keep a secret or spill it, and talk about hunches, distraction and how things turn out.

stages.name: Stage 4
stages.summary: Talk about worry, embarrassment and being swamped, close and distant relationships, lies and comebacks, gambles and blunders, and whether something was worth the money.
